newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary cenbank says depo changes protect savings.
newsitem.headline: Hungary cenbank says depo changes protect savings.

text.p: The National Bank of Hungary said the changes it implemented in its deposit system on Monday were designed to protect domestic savings.

"With the 0.25 percent correction in the six-month deposit facility and the introduction of the 12-month deposit facility, the NBH wants to increase its support to domestic financial savings," the NBH said in a statement.

The NBH earlier on Monday raised the interest rates it offers to commercial banks on their six-month deposits by a quarter percentage point to 21.00 percent, reversing a trend of almost regular monthly central bank rate cuts in the past few months.
The NBH also announced earlier on Monday that it launched a 12-month deposit facility at an annual 20.50 percent rate.

The NBH said in the statement that the protection of savings and current market interest rate levels was necessary because the decline of interest rates in the past few months might block the expected improvement in economic processes.

"Current interest rate levels, or their further decline do not encourage savings sufficiently, and for the long term may jeopardise further favourable changes in inflation and macroeconomic processes," the NBH said.
The central bank added that it was preparing to launch NBH securities, which would be offered not only to banks but also to other financial investors and individuals.
With the introduction of the new securities, the central bank wishes to ensure appropriate yield levels for small investors, the NBH said.
Hungary expects inflation to go down to 17 percent year-on-year by December from the current 18.8 percent level.
